Context/Background:
Prostate cancer (PCa) is the second leading cause of male cancer-related deaths. To date, the strategy to develop therapies for PCa mainly focuses on blocking either the activity or the transcriptional targets of known oncogenes. While the PCa transcriptome has been studied for decades, we have little knowledge of the translatome. The importance of this post-transcriptional regulation is underscored by the realization that RNA transcript levels are a poor proxy for protein abundance.

Translation initiation is a tightly regulated step critical to maintain the accurate protein dosage of growth and survival factors in cells.Importantly, emerging studies show that translation factors act in a rapid, selective, and robust manner to control the production of specific proteins. One of the most important of those factors is the RNA-binding protein and translation factor eukaryotic initiation factor 4A (eIF4A), which helps to unwind structured 5′ UTRs to increase translation initiation of select mRNAs in cancer.

Pharmacologic inhibition of eIF4A with zotatifin, a clinical compound, suppressed tumor growth in vivo, reducing both primary tumor growth and metastasis.

To understand how the inhibitor works mechanistically, we investigated the effect of zotatifin on the PCa translatome and proteome after a short treatment, as translation is one of the most rapid steps of gene expression. We performed ribosome profiling (Ribo-seq) and MS after 6 h of zotatifin treatment in 22Rv1 cell xenografts in vivo. While MS analysis assesses the effect of zotatifin on the global protein landscape in tumors, Ribo-seq can capture translation efficiency genome-wide at single-nucleotide resolution. Ribo-seq analysis revealed 554 downregulated transcripts at the translational level (false discovery rate [FDR] < 0.01 and log2FC ≤ −0.3). On the other hand, MS analysis showed that 339 proteins were downregulated upon zotatifin treatment (p value < 0.05 and log2FC ≤ −0.2). Next, we analyzed genes that are downregulated at the translational level as well as at the protein level by cross-referencing the two datasets using less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 and log2FC < 0 and MS p value < 0.05 and log2(FC) < 0).
Prompt: From the genes that are downregulated at both translational level and protein level, prioritize a few targets that are particularly relevant to prostate cancer.
output_text:
Introduction/Context  
Zotatifin, a clinical eIF4A inhibitor, was tested on 22Rv1 prostate cancer cell xenografts in vivo. After 6 h treatment, Ribo-seq identified 554 transcripts downregulated at the translational level (FDR < 0.01, log2FC ≤ −0.3) and MS detected 339 proteins downregulated (p < 0.05, log2FC ≤ −0.2). Using less stringent cutoffs (Ribo-seq FDR < 0.05 & log2FC < 0; MS p < 0.05 & log2FC < 0), 108 genes were concordantly downregulated at both levels.  

Keywords  
• Translation initiation  
• eIF4A inhibition  
• Hypoxia signaling  
• PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway  
• Androgen signaling  

Candidate Genes  
HIF1A, PDCD4, AR, PIK3CA, TPX2, RAD21

Analysis  
Overall, zotatifin triggers a broad down-regulation of cell-cycle, signaling and metabolic programs, reflected by the dominance of negative enrichments in cell-cycle (G2/M checkpoint), PI3K/AKT/mTOR, mTORC1 signaling, E2F targets and glycolysis/hypoxia hallmarks. Only Estrogen Response Early showed modest up-regulation. Key cancer-related pathways (Proteoglycans in cancer; Prostate cancer; PI3K AKT Signaling in Cancer) appear in both ORA and GSEA, underscoring disruption of oncogenic signaling. The convergence on hypoxia (HIF1A), androgen signaling (AR) and translational control (PDCD4) suggests that zotatifin attenuates both the production and activity of critical PCa drivers.  

Targeted (keyword-guided) subset  
ORA “Prostate cancer” (MSigDB_Hallmark_2020): AR; GSK3B; PIK3CA  
GSEA “Prostate cancer” (KEGG_2016): PDGFB; CCNE1; CREB3; RAF1; CTNNB1; AR; PIK3CG; GSK3B; PTEN; PIK3R1; IGF1R; GRB2; PIK3CD; PIK3R3; FGFR1; NFKB1; PDGFC; LEF1; PIK3CB; MAP2K1; MDM2; PIK3CA  

Key Genes/Proteins (leading-edge)  

Downregulated targets:  
| Gene    | Direction | Role/Function                                                    | Pathway(s)                                                  |
|---------|-----------|------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| AR      | DOWN      | Androgen receptor; nuclear transcription factor driving PCa growth | Prostate cancer; G2/M checkpoint; PI3K/AKT/mTOR            |
| HIF1A   | DOWN      | Hypoxia-inducible transcription factor                           | Hypoxia; mTORC1 signaling; central carbon metabolism       |
| PDCD4   | DOWN      | Tumor suppressor; binds eIF4A to inhibit translation             | Proteoglycans in cancer; translation initiation            |
| PIK3CA  | DOWN      | Catalytic α subunit of PI3K; mediates PI3K/AKT signaling         | PI3K/AKT/mTOR; multiple cancer pathways                    |
| TPX2    | DOWN      | Microtubule nucleation factor                                    | Mitotic spindle; G2/M checkpoint                           |
| RAD21   | DOWN      | Cohesin complex component; chromatid cohesion, DNA repair        | DNA replication/repair; mitotic spindle                    |

Comparisons  
• AR, HIF1A and PDCD4 were downregulated in both Ribo-seq (FDR < 1e-6 for AR; PDCD4 in multiple hallmarks) and MS (p < 0.01), highlighting robust cross-modality hits.  
• PI3K pathway components (PIK3CA/GSK3B) appear in GSEA, ORA and leading-edge gene tables, underscoring strong attenuation of proliferative signaling.  
• Cell-cycle factors (TPX2, RAD21) map to G2/M and mitotic spindle terms, reflecting a halt in proliferation.  

Implications  
Zotatifin dampens eIF4A-dependent translation of key oncogenic drivers (AR, HIF1A, PDCD4), leading to down-regulation of hypoxia adaptation, androgen signaling and cell-cycle progression. Suppression of PI3K/AKT/mTOR and G2/M pathways may underlie its antitumor efficacy in PCa. PDCD4 down-regulation may both reflect and enhance translational control feedback loops.  

Next Steps & Clarifications  
1. Validate protein-level decreases of AR, HIF1A and PDCD4 by western blot in 22Rv1 xenografts.  
2. Assess whether combinatorial targeting of PI3K/AKT/mTOR potentiates zotatifin’s effects.  
3. Measure changes in cell-cycle distribution and mitotic markers to confirm G2/M arrest.  
4. Examine longer zotatifin exposures to capture secondary adaptive responses (e.g., stress and immune pathways).
